title: SC issues notice to CJP, Congress, AAP, AISA on traders’ plea against Delhi protests

ai.summary: The Supreme Court has issued notices to political parties and organisations regarding a petition by Delhi traders challenging the police designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue, citing disruptions to business and livelihoods during festive season.

facts.claim: The Supreme Court issued notices to political parties and organisations on a petition by Delhi traders challenging the police designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue
facts.quote: A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant issued notices on a petition filed by the Kirana Committee of Delhi

facts.claim: The petition argues that demonstrations at Ramlila Maidan disrupt business, affect livelihoods, and deny access to roads leading to nearby residential areas
facts.quote: The traders have argued that demonstrations at the ground disrupt business, affect livelihoods and deny access to roads leading to nearby residential areas.

facts.claim: The petition estimated that Delhi sees daily business of around ₹500 crore to ₹600 crore, with about ₹250 crore at risk each day during peak season between October 2026 and January 2027
facts.quote: It estimated that Delhi sees daily business of around ₹500 crore to ₹600 crore, of which about ₹250 crore was at risk each day during the peak season between October 2026 and January 2027.

facts.claim: The petition said nearly one million establishments, 10 million livelihoods and around 500,000 outstation traders depended on this activity
facts.quote: The petition said nearly one million establishments, 10 million livelihoods and around 500,000 outstation traders depended on this activity.

ai.background_note: The petition challenges Delhi Police's designation of Ramlila Maidan as a protest venue, citing disruptions to business and livelihoods during festive season, and seeks a framework for protests that considers the impact on residents and businesses.
